title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1986 'Analysis situs' manuscript, where Grothendieck axiomatizes 'ateliers' (workshops) of tame, multistratified figures. The primitive data are a set M of 'figures' or pieces with:
- an inclusion order ≤;
- a 'well-inside' relation X' ≪ X (X' relatively compact or interior in X);
- a disjointness relation X ∥ Y;
- a 'compatibility' or proper-intersection relation, written F ≷ G (the transcription misreads it as ≱).
The intersection L = F ∩ G is not set-theoretic. It is the lattice supremum of the strata Z lying below both F and G. For X' ≪ X, the symbol X'_L denotes the part of X' lying in L, through its pieces X'' ≤ X' with X'' ≪ L.

The page states a weakened form of the previous page's Property 1.

Property 1'_0. Let F ≷ G (compatible), F' ≪ F, G' ≪ G and L = F ∩ G. Then F' ∥ G' ⟺ F'_L ∥ G'_L.
- (⇒) is automatic, since disjointness is inherited by subfigures.
- (⇐) is equivalent to the atelier axiom At CD 1'_0: for X ≷ Y in M with X' ≪ X, Y' ≪ Y and L = X ∩ Y, suppose all X'' ≤ X', Y'' ≤ Y' with X'', Y'' ≪ L are disjoint. Then X' ∥ Y'.
- In words: for compatibly intersecting figures, disjointness of shrunken pieces can be tested on their traces along the intersection. It is a locality principle for disjointness.

Corollaries:
- Cor. 1: Property 1' holds.
- Cor. 2: if F ≷ G, F' ≪ F and F'_L = ∅, then F' is disjoint from the shrinkings G' of G.
- Cor. 3: F ∥ G ⇒ F' ∥ G' for all F' ≪ F, G' ≪ G.
- Margin Cor. 4: F'_L = ∅ ⟺ F' ∥ L.
Grothendieck adds that he tends to regard At CD as an 'obligatory axiom' for the theories.

Property 2 ('ateliers spéciaux'). This is a converse criterion for compatibility. Compatibility of F, G is not assumed. Let L = sup of the strata Z ≤ F, G. Suppose every F' ≪ F avoiding L (F'_L = ∅) is disjoint from every G' ≪ G avoiding L. Then F ≷ G.
- In words: if two figures are disjoint away from their lattice intersection, they intersect compatibly.
- The margin calls this a 'critère de disjonction par les voisinages tubulaires'.
- The next page shows this fails for 'polyidéaux' ateliers. There Grothendieck adds the hypothesis L ∈ M (variant At CD 2').

Purpose: to build ateliers from the data (M, ≤, ≪, ∥) alone, with compatibility characterized through disjointness.
errors: No clear mathematical error. (⇒) of Property 1'_0 relies on disjointness being hereditary under ≤, which is implicitly assumed.

Cor. 2 is stated loosely: 'disjoint de tout voisinage G' de G' mixes 'neighbourhood' language with the relation G' ≪ G (a shrinking, not a neighbourhood). The intended meaning is presumably disjoint from every G' ≪ G.
Property 2 is not valid in general, as Grothendieck himself notes on the next page (it fails for polyideal ateliers). It is a defining axiom of the 'special' class, not a theorem.

ideas.what: Locality axiom: disjointness of shrunken pieces of compatibly intersecting figures can be tested on their traces along the intersection (At CD 1'_0)
ideas.modern_name: local criterion for disjointness / separation in a tame-topology or o-minimal-style axiomatics; analogous to axioms of contact algebras (mereotopology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no direct counterpart; mereotopology/contact algebras (de Vries 1962, Whitehead-style region calculi; later Düntsch–Vakarelov) use similar ≪ and contact relations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches 'topologie modérée'; the atelier axiomatics is unpublished

ideas.what: Criterion for compatibility (proper intersection) of figures via disjointness of shrinkings that avoid the lattice intersection (Property 2, 'ateliers spéciaux')
ideas.modern_name: characterizing clean intersection via separation away from the intersection; tubular-neighbourhood style criterion

ideas.what: Corollaries: disjoint figures have disjoint shrinkings; a shrinking avoiding L is disjoint from shrinkings of the other figure

missed.claim: The data (M, ≤, ≪, ∥), with intersection defined as a lattice supremum, closely resembles point-free mereotopology: de Vries compingent algebras and the contact/region-connection calculi (well-inside relation, disjointness/contact). Grothendieck's axioms are a tame, stratified analogue. The link between his 'ateliers' program for tame topology and contact-algebra / point-free topology seems unexplored.
missed.quote: Ax CD 1'_0 ... supposons que X'_L ∥ Y'_L (i.e. ∀ X'', Y'' ∈ M, X'' ≤ X', Y'' ≤ Y', X'' ≪ L, Y'' ≪ L, on ait X'' ∥ Y'') Alors X' ∥ Y'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give a point-free axiomatization of o-minimal or tame topology, of interest to model theory and to tame geometry.

missed.claim: The 'atelier' axiom system, with the dichotomy between special ateliers (At CD 2) and polyideal ateliers (At CD 2'), is an unpublished axiomatics of tame topology that was never developed in the literature.
missed.quote: J'ai tendance à regarder Ax CD comme 'axiome obligatoire' pour les théories.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Its axioms could be compared with o-minimal structures and definable stratifications to see whether they characterize them.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a detailed working page of an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology project. The individual statements are elementary, but the axiomatics as a whole is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The relation written '≱' (F ≱ G, X ≱ Y) is in fact the compatibility symbol '≷'/'⋚' (the one used on page 10). Property 2 concludes 'Alors F ≷ G'.
'Ax CD' should read 'At CD' (atelier axioms), consistent with the neighbouring pages.
'Propriété 2 (des "tubes spéciaux")' more likely reads '(des "ateliers spéciaux")'. The struck heading is likewise 'Axiome des ateliers spéciaux', consistent with page 10's margin.
Left margin: likely 'Critère de disjonction par les voisinages tubulaires de sous-figures'.
The NB after Ax CD 1'_0 likely reads '(NB ceci équivaut aussi, [en présence de?], à At CD 1')'.
